fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. The city held on to the ways of two old kings and took their advice too. Omri, a king of Israel, did evil in the sight of the LORD (1 Kings 16:25). His son Ahab did evil too (1 Kings 16:30). Those were the role models this city picked.

Not quite, friend. Nothing gets torn down or burned in this verse. The city hung on to the ways of Omri, a king of Israel, and of his son Ahab. Both of them did evil in the sight of the LORD (1 Kings 16:25, 30). The city was holding that stuff close.

I wish that were true, baker, but the verse says otherwise. These old ways were still alive in the city, and people were still listening to that advice. Omri was a king of Israel, and his son Ahab reigned in his place (1 Kings 16:25, 28). Nobody had forgotten them. They were still being followed.
